newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: JCI unit buys Shell S.Africa coal business.
newsitem.headline: JCI unit buys Shell S.Africa coal business.

text.p: South African mining house JCI Ltd said on Tuesday its wholly-owned subsidiary Tavistock Colliery Ltd had acquired the entire coal business of Shell South Africa for 440 million rand.
The transaction is with effect from January 1, 1997.
JCI said that Ingwe Coal Corporation Ltd has the pre-emptive right of the Rietspruit coal business of Shell South Africa.
Shell South Africa is a unit of Royal Dutch/Shell.

JCI said the balance of the purchase consideration, which pertained to Rietspruit, is payable by Tavistock to Shell South Africa upon receipt of the notification from Ingwe that it will not exercise the pre-emptive right.
JCI managing director Bill Nairn said the deal underscored the company's commitment to grow its assets -- particularly those in commodities.

"The acquisition of the coal assets of Shell South Africa, in particular the RBCT (Richards Bay Coal Terminal) entitlement, will increase export potential and with the larger resource base, will lead to the development of new mines," Nairn said.

Shell's coal business in South Africa comprises a 6.827 percent share in the Richards Bay terminal and around 1,75 million tonnes of in situ coal reserves and certain surface rights in Mpumalanga province and northern Free State province.

"The acquisition expands and diversifies Tavistock's production base. This will allow for greater production flexibility and improved scheduling of growth to enable Tavistock to respond better to the demands of the local and international coal market," JCI said.

It said Shell's established presence in the international coal industry will assist Tavistock in securing new markets while an agency agreement had been entered into with Shell in respect of Rietspruit coal.
Analysts said earlier this year that JCI's planned purchase of Shell South Africa's coal interests signalled its emergence as a key player in the coal export industry.
Shell said in February that it had signed a letter of intent to sell its coal interests in South Africa.
The company said it would concentrate on the core elements of its coal business in Australia and Venezuela.
On Tuesday, Shell South Africa said the sale was a "natural fit with the JCI coal assets and will enable the combined business to realise considerable synergies".
Shell South Africa chief executive John Drake said in a statement that the decision to sell was based on purely commercial considerations.
"However, Shell was pleased that the purchaser is a group in which there will be a major black South African shareholding," Drake added.
